data.heading: Muscular system
data.text: There are more than six hundred muscles in the human body.
Muscles are elastic by nature. They can contract and expand.
Muscles that you can control are called voluntary muscles.
Muscles that function on their own are known as involuntary muscles.
Skeletal muscles are attached to your bones by fibres known as tendons.
Smooth muscles are involuntary muscles which keep your body systems going.
Smooth muscles in the digestive system contract and expand to help in the digestion of food.
Smooth muscles in the eyes help you to see properly by controlling the size of the pupils.
Muscles in the heart are called cardiac muscles.
